title: A month on Maui
summary: Gil describes walking ten miles a day on Maui and the island's imported plants and animals.

blocks.x: So that's what I mean by balance. To get away and enjoy, enjoy the land and the water and all things like that. We spent a month in Maui (?).
I know it's one of the Hawaiian Islands.

Coming home from Tokyo. We re-routed the tickets and it didn't cost any more to stop in Maui. So we spent the money that I had there because we didn't want to be in New York in the hot weather. It was a wonderful experience.
I didn't have a driver's licence so, I couldn't rent a car there. Everybody had cars you know. You have

to have one. Well I let my driver's licence go since I've been in New York even though I drove from the time I was thirteen years old, in the West you know, you have to drive. Anyway, I had to walk all the time there. So I walked into town. I walked around some places near the beach.
You went from the sublime to the ridiculous and back to the sublime. (LAUGHTER).
That's it, once a day I walked ten miles. And I could smell the land and could hear it and whistle. It was an experience.

The Hawaiian Islands are, they are a flora paradise you know. Flowers and trees and hedges and birds and a few (fields of pineapples?). And a lot of it, more than half of it is imported and planted there. Brought from other places. A lot of the vegetation happens to work in the Hawaiian Islands but it's not native to there. And some of the animals like the mongoose was brought there, it was from India, not a native.
There are no really indigenous animals, oh the wild boar which was probably brought from somewhere else too, I guess.
